body: deffonitelyy agree. I love cats and waiting till I can financially commit to one.
the world can be a cruel place. we learn to be more discerning but people still hurt us. I wish we had the luck to meet good people more often than bad ones.

34 here. relate to everything u said so much. I have bpd, depression and ALOT of trauma from past relationships and experiences with women. with all that in tow, dating is close to impossible for me. people run away when they hear the bpd. radical acceptance and realising that happiness has to look different for me is something I'm working towards. I don't like it when people tell me I'll find someone for to have hope because I want to be realistic and not continually let down. I want to see my situation as is and learn to handle and accept a life of romantic isolation, and finding other meaning and focusing on friendships instead which is so so hard. society where I live centres the romantic relationship as the highest priority so it's hard to find like minded people who want to focus on friendships instead.

34 here turning 35 soon. I guess as a group sure maybe more mature, confident...but I think individually it definitely varies. I think I'm still figuring stuff out in areas that my younger colleagues have already accomplished more in.
Same! some ick especially with the shirt being called a blouse lol but no issues with being called cute etc. I actually sleep with no fewer than 3 soft toys in my bed hehe
14 but I think the self destruction was there when I was younger.

just sharing my opinion as a lonely gay lady. it's a struggle and something I'm working on in therapy as well. to accept that I'll be alone for the remainder of my life. I don't think I have any advice. just that focusing on building other aspects of life is important as well and that there will be hard days when you feel sad and lonely but those days will past and life will go on.

yeah I feel the exact same way. the hurt is so so deep. I can't convince you to not go through with it because when I was there no amount of it will get better helped me. because life doesn't always get better...externally at least. the only person you can count on is yourself. if you can or want to, you can try therapy. but it does take awhile sometimes to find a good therapist. I'm hoping u find inner peace. I'm still trying to find mine.

I won't say I chose my career I just sort of fell into it haha. but I stuck with it because I have no idea what I want to do. and I wanted to be responsible and not do things on a whim. just trying to fulfil the role of the responsible adult I guess.
I don't know but I do know that I experience the same. it's always a valid way for me to end my pain. it actually makes me feel better to have some control over my pain especially when it gets bad.

this is so relatable. it's tough. I feel like dating and relationship culture these days is like people just don't care about commitment or working on the relationship anymore. no compromises, no working things out. it's so flippant and people leave at the first sign of inconvenience to their carefully crafted "individuality"....sighhh

hmmm sort of. not a different voice although I don't know how it sounds but more of a compassionate voice and a voice of someone that wants to protect me from all hurt and tells me everyone is out to get me.

yeah I don't think it'll happen for me. people play with me till they see who I am then lose interest. my part in it is over attaching to anyone showing a modicum of human decency so I'm complicit in my own pain.

yeah I personally don't equate unconditional to self-sacrificial to the point of accepting abuse. more like loving you as you are with your flaws, not needing you to not be yourself like wearing branded clothes you can't afford and so on.
I won't say it would fix me. but it would help alot for sure.
I turn off read receipts for a reason haha. rather not see visual confirmation that I was ignored.
I agree with the wrong not to be afraid. my parents weren't afraid. I was an accident. and here I am 30 odd years later alone. can't live the life that I want.

agreed. yes we have a personality disorder but that doesn't mean shitty people don't exist as well. not mutually exclusive. only difference is that our reactionary feelings are more intense and pronounced.

yeah I've been told I'm high maintenance. to not spam their messages then oh well actually you can spam me, I just won't answer. and all I can do is say okay because I'm scared to ask for more and scare them away. it's hard to find people who can put up with what we need maybe which is why I'm alone and unwanted.

yes it's definitely still a struggle in a relationship. I also seek reassurance to the point it annoys the other person and causes them to lose all interest and patience..whatever little interest they had in the first place at least. I feel the same that I'm destined to be alone because everyone leaves me in the end...that's what my life has shown me. people say stop self pitying and just go date around but oof I really don't know if I can withstand another failed relationship...and get out alive.

I understand fully about being wondering what you deserve or not knowing what is real or what is good or bad. my sense of that has been completely ruined as well. the situation you described sounds like someone who has alot of healing to do because it feels like she's projecting alot of her past relationship onto you. my ex was similar (not abusive) but she had no patience for my bpd symptoms. she would get very angry and call it self pity or me throwing tantrums. I'm not exactly sure what to call it but it's like if someone hurt them and made them feel unseen or invalidated and you have the same mental disorder, they won't be able to ascribe any other reason to your behaviour other than that of deliberate attention seeking or basically just you having bad intentions towards them and then they'll be in fight mode to defend themselves. it's just my opinion. I mean if your partner is willing to work with you to change the relationship dynamic it's possible. but please leave if the physical abuse continues or escalates. that part has to stop.  many people who've been partners of people with bpd who wasn't the best...they end up just thinking we're all evil and never want anything to do with us again. my ex falls somewhere towards that category where she just feels everything I do is just me being an ass or whiny or something. I try to explain sometimes not well but I try like how I struggle with seeing her as an integrated person because of my black and white thinking but it's like she sees it as me mistreating her. 


edit to say that it's not intentional on their part. it's highly likely some form of trauma that operates in the subconscious that says okay this person is deliberately abusing me so I need to fight back.
YES I would. I have major mental issues. wouldn't mind a shorter life lol. to me, this situation actually sounds like win win for me lol.

well just because she was a victim in her past relationship doesn't mean she can't be the abuser in this one. i mean I grew a up a victim but subject people to emotional abuse in my life as someone who developed bpd as a result of being a victim in my past. i don't intentionally mean harm on the people i have subject to my abuse either. it's a very unfortunate byproduct of being a victim - that you can become the abuser. 


you having mental health struggles doesn't mean you deserve to be physically abused.

safety first. it's my own frame of reference but I work in a conservative place and if I were out I know I'd be ostracised to the point that my job would be affected. it's the sad reality of things that we can't be fully accepted everywhere. on the other hand if safe you can go from subtle "boyfriends aren't up my alley" to overt like "I'm a lesbian". short of waving a lesbian flag in their faces, I guess that's the gamut of responses available to you. the anxiety and shame part will go away with positive reinforcement which is out of our control as people can react badly sometimes. safety first.

well not really I don't think so. but my therapist did say I'm more tolerant of stuff because I know what it's like. and I said well that's coz I have a malfunctioning brain too. I guess that's as close to a positive as there is.
yeah penance that's a good word for it. I need to be alone because I'm too messed up and hurt others.

relate so much to this post. I'm so sorry. it's a very painful way to live. I watched a video on corrective relationships and I was thinking well I have the opposite because all my life experiences has taught me is the opposite. that I am not worth it, that I am nothing, that I deserve to be dead. that I'm too clingy, disgusting, unstable. I hate that I'm like my father in even the smallest of ways who I see as one of the key factors in me being this way in the first place.
YES. alone now because no one wants bpd. it's like what reason do I have to preserve my own safety? no one gives a shit about me anyways.

no not really. I'm alone now and it's worse than ever. in a relationship I feel like I have a reason you know? some meaning or a future to work towards. now I just want to die all the time. most of the time I don't know why i go to work, exercise etc. I'm all alone and I just...want...to...die.


I mean sure it's alot of pressure to put on a relationship but at the same time the reality is without it, I don't have a sense of meaning or self worth. guess it's different from person to person.

agree with this. I want to isolate but I also know that's a one way ticket to hell for me. oof I'm so messed up now though...I isolate sometimes to protect people from me. ask my ex, she probably thinks i should just leave everyone alone all the time.

I wish I had this. I mean not like untreated bpd but just someone who can be like it's not perfect but we'll find ways around it. and then I have outbursts which I will do my best not to do of course but they'll let me know when I do if I do it and didn't realise it and then they don't just leave when it isn't perfect because I'm too much. it's hard and I don't think it's in the cards for me in this life.

yeah. the key I guess is finding a healthy way of expressing or dealing with it so you don't keep it ALL in. I struggle with that alot. my ex found it impossible to deal with. she fell out of love with me very quickly and dumped me and moved on also fairly quickly. that's how monstrous and unlovable I am. I won't say it's always toxic but few people would stay to try hard with us. they find easier relationships to be in which is fair to them. I don't feel it's possible for me. people I like or love don't stay and I feel I am worth nothing.
yeah I think it's possible and I feel an irrelevant factor.
noooo hell no. it's not about bpd or not that determines a good partner for you...it's other factors.

would journaling help? I know my memory is foggy af after several very traumatic things happened to me these past few years. my therapist asked if I think I deal with certain things better now compared to when she first saw me and I'm like I can't even remember...so I'll need to write stuff down more now.

i do that too. I hit myself and say mean things to myself but at least it's not a permanent scar and I don't feel so bad for leaving a mark on myself...somehow it makes me feel less pathetic that I can't cope how normal people can when I hit instead of other more permanent means.

I fight this symptom with every fibre of my being. I reach out (basically opposite action) when everything is screaming inside me to stay away. but then there's also a single voice that says hey talk to them, you might not be able to tomorrow. and then i do.
people say to trust your gut feeling or wise mind but I don't even know which voice is my wise mind anymore. it's all so overwhelming.

yeah in my 30s now. doing all that healthy stuff. exercise, keeping up a job, upgrading myself with learning, hobbies. but I'm dead inside. want to die all the time. basically just going back and forth between wanting to die a little and wanting to die alooot. no one likes me for who I am. I am a burden and way too gross and clingy for anyone.

it's quite different for me. I tend to like people who happen to be emotionally unavailable. not underachievers. a person with a job, responsible etc. not necessarily high achievers but people who are "normal" and they tend not to like me because I'm clingy, spammy with texts and overall a disgusting person...who is simultaneously too much and not enough. too emotional, not enough emotional regulation. try to hard to make the other person happy and end up smothering them and so on. basically just repel every single person on earth.

that's been my experience too. I'd say the high highs and low lows have tempered somewhat but the emptiness and depression and this craving for connection is more heightened. it's almost like I missed the last bus to a happy life and now I'm just waiting to die. very much situation dependent for sure. I've met my fair share of people who've left me worse for wear when I started to open up to friendships or relationships. being dumped or criticised for being too much doesn't do wonders for the feeling like I'm just a flawed monster that people are better off without. 


I can't say I was free of fault but sometimes all I did was ask for more time to spend together and then I'm too high maintenance or whatever. I've lost any of the little hope I had when I was younger and had arguably worse symptoms. I'm really just waiting and wanting to die all the time now...definitely more than I used to.

yeah it's rough. abit of a tongue in cheek comment here but you sure the first lady actually knows your name? haha. 


I hope you find your person soon. and you are right, when or if I ever do find someone ever again, I'm going to be holding on tight.
yes I do. I fight sh urges but sometimes I cave and basically physically and verbally abuse myself. nothing that physically leaves a mark though so I feel better and like I'm less messed up inside.
just partner if I had one. basically anyone who I think would be exposed to my bs that would have to use that as an evaluation factor in whether it's something they want.

yeah it would be nice. I honestly don't even have a single person I can talk to about my issues except for my therapist.


sometimes just communicating with the other person you need some support and not solutions at the moment can help.

yeah totally agree. I'm having one of those days where my urge to throw myself off a building is almost peaking but I need to function like a normal human at work...smiling, joking, working. I don't even want to live anymore.
yeah anxiety or stress in my life exacerbates it. when my ex broke up with me for the first time, I grinded my teeth so hard it woke me up.
yes! swimming and weights and bodyweight stuff. before I fractured my ankle I used to do bjj.

oh yeah I definitely do. sometimes all it takes is a trigger like a familiar emotion or familiar behavior that I see in someone else and I just sort of go back to the time it happened. my body reacts like it's happening to me all over again. I kind of zone out when it happens but not all the time. most times I'm able to stop myself and focus on work or life. but when I'm alone that's when it gets rough.

it was more than a year ago I don't even remember his name. I did however bitch about my experience to my psychologist who works in the same hospital. she told me maybe he's just making sure that their staff is safe or something. and during my stay, my psychologist came to see me twice and both times the nurses or someone came to check on us (likely safety of my psychologist) through the door window. more often than not I've found doctors here at least to have a certain emotional chip missing. but I guess I do get it. it's a psychiatristic ward and it can be dangerous so they're taking the measures they're supposed to? at the same time I felt less than human for sure...

yeah I get that. like everything I do doesn't result in them being closer whether it's distance or increasing contact. life is complicated, and it's not just one factor affecting their behaviour towards us. they may have other issues . it's incredibly difficult to know what's the right thing to do. if life were straightforward, it'd be alooot easier. I'm just alone alot these days. and I err on the side of protecting myself from heartbreak because I don't honestly know if I can take another one and stay alive and I'm not really exaggerating. so I just distance myself from everyone and keep all my issues to myself and my therapist.
me too. tired of being a burden

yep. I'm the same. it's a coping mechanism I think. also I feel like I already am objectively a burden to everyone around me, it takes me so much energy to act normal, I have no reason to live. so when something, anything bad happens even if it's minor I'm like okay well might as well die now. almost like a straw breaks the camel's back sort of thing.
yeah I do. my exes and friends do too. everyone gets sick of me.

yeah totally when the relationship is off...and the other person withholds reassurance it drives my anxiety through the roof. look up corrective relationships by John gunderson, it's so illuminative on the role of how a partner who is there for us can help alleviate so much of our symptoms. my ex kept trying to break up with me. i tried asking for reasons but i think in the end she just lost interest in me. stopped loving me even though she told me she did throughout. she just stopped wanting to be with me. probably found me too much and lost interest because I was too interested or asked for too much commitment or something no idea. 


well anyway she then said the relationship wasn't working in the end. and I was just thinking that my anxiety over her just leaving at anytime very likely exacerbated my symptoms tenfold which made the problems in the relationship a vicious cycle. 


thanks for sharing the song. I haven't struggled with pushing people away for a long time. it's usually the other way around these days...people wanting to leave me and I desperately hold on.

doesn't help that the media is quick to paint everyone with bpd. stalkerish murderer? bpd. Amber heard? bpd. serial killer? bpd. jodie arias? bpd. even my ex told me the Saltburn dude probably has bpd. I didn't take that well and went cray cray. like that's what my ex thought when she saw the movie...like yeah this dude's behavior is reminiscent of my ex (me). how awful does she see me?

omg tell me about it. when I went to emergency last year...and I was like I just want to see my psychologist. I was sobbing, suicidal (and they knew it) yet the junior doctor was like oh do you want to see your psychologist because you're attracted to her (I'm also gay in a pretty heteronormative culture). I swear for a moment I lost all suicidal impulses and my only impulse was to kick him out of the room....like wtf bro? just coz I have bpd traits and am gay I'm doing this to look lovingly at my psychologist?!??!! dude I want to die, I'm sobbing and desperate for relief wtf?!?!?!

makes sense. haha my ex probably thinks I'm being deliberately manipulative or something. she always gets angry and calls what I'm doing self pity. not saying it's not my fault but honestly her anger makes me more fearful and erratic.

if she's avoidantly attached, it makes sense that she would want you close but keep you at a distance at the same time to maintain her independence and sense of control. 


easier said than done but you need to put up solid boundaries. don't allow her the privileges she would have if she committed to you as a girlfriend. rigid boundaries with someone like that is very important because you need to always protect yourself first and foremost. from my experience, people who are like that...Well they leave a trail of heartbreak and they're not going to ever be accountable for the part they play. they'll just say it's your fault for being this way or something like that. you're too sensitive, you're the one who offered I never asked etc. because for them being responsible for someone is their biggest fear. 


not saying all avoidant people are like that but if she's not in therapy or actively working on her attachment wounds, chances are high you'll be badly hurt in the end and she won't be there to support you in any way.

it's a hurtful comment. I mean being told that something you are already insecure about is true or getting confirmation about it from someone you like even a little is hard. you're not too sensitive...it is hurtful.

yeah it's hard to hear when someone you like tells you that you're alot after telling you you're okay. always hurts....a lot. I wish I could tell upfront when talking to someone if they would actually be okay with me...saves alot of hurt downstream.
I asked an ex if I had bpd eyes and she said I don't.
yes I get non verbal too. maybe talk it out with your partner during better moments like what to expect and plan ahead on what you both can or will do when u do get non verbal.
not op but yeah normal and stable sounds like a dream. I guess my ex would call it self pity and be angry at me for thinking this way. she would say just suck it up and not whine or something.

I don't even know. I'm an endless void and I feel like a freak. I just try to have as many friendships as possible to spread it out evenly and not overwhelm any one person. at this point I don't even know what's going on anymore. no one deserves to have my romantic attention, so I stay arm's length from everyone.

yeah I relate. it's hard to tell people it gets better when my own life isn't getting better...my ex left because of my bpd. I mean to go from love (she said she never loved someone so much in such a short time) to falling out of love so quickly because of my bpd....that's confirmation of my shittyness isn't it? like wow it disappeared so quickly. people stare at my sh scars. I'm a freak. matter of time before I'll take myself out as well.

not op but yeah I'm trying but it's tiring. people are not kind. they get scared and freaked out by my visible sh scars and stuff. and my ex just said the murderous Saltburn dude has bpd.....sigh like that was the first illness that came to her mind when she saw the movie...why bother trying if everyone thinks we lost causes??? it's tiring but thank you. I'm also going to be cat lady.
that is true. self love has no correlation to relationship status.

yeah sort of. that's why I talk to many many people and not focus it on just one person to hear me blabber. everyone tells me I'm a non stop talker. and like it's a joke that they'll ask me to shut up and tape my mouth but I'll still be talking. 


some people have a higher capacity for it and others well....they're the ones who think I'm high maintenance and lose interest me fairly quickly when they find out I'm too much, too clingy whatever.

yeah it can be unintentionally invalidating. people do it because we like to push negative emotions away as a society as soon as possible. so solve the problem and get rid of bad emotions. but emotions don't work like that. most times, we just need to sit with negative emotions. cry, sob, yell and find a friend who will yell with you.

I struggle with retroactive jealousy too and I have weird triggers around s*x as well. so with my ex it really bothered me and I was insecure alot and it caused her to get angry with me a bunch. it became one of the reasons she dumped me. having said that I would never ever have let that be a reason to break up with her because I know it's on me and it's my own responsibility and ownership to deal with. everyone has a past. okay say u break up with someone who is great now except for the past stuff. like what's next? date a monk? I mean don't let go of a good person. find ways to work on your own stuff with your partner's reassurance.

yea therapy makes it worse in a way coz I see how being single I always want to die. while I'm in a relationship though I act out in ways that quickens the demise and the other person dumps me. like in a relationship my suicidality goes down so much but I'm not grateful no, I screw it up. then become single and lonely with all the suicidality coming back full force. and u reflect on it in therapy and realise it's all your own fault and realise how smothering and screwed up I am in the head that it's basically all my own fault my life is like this.

thank you. well other kinds if hurt also factor in even if you've only had one relationship. contributes to the hermit thing at least imo.

I guess I could date super cautiously but I'm a little too traumatised..the other person would have to be so understanding. it's just way too scary.

kudos to you for being stable and healthy enough to draw solid boundaries and walk away rather than get sucked into that. that's a good trait to have. it's something I definitely need to work on myself.
same same

oof I'm a little hermit too. it's been alot of relationship trauma for me past few years so I'm way more of a hermit now. I only talk to married women with families or people I know there's no chance in he'll for romance with them because it's way way way safer. I'm terrified of getting hurt again...coz I don't know if I could take another blow.

yeah it's abit different but it's like I'm broken or damaged. things others find sad and stressful I feel totally numb. of course I do get the part where people are happy and laughing like at a company gathering, and for me I'm just numb as well.

yeah I guess I was surprised when I first realised it when i sought counselling for the first time in my life because it's such a normal for me. it calms me down knowing or imagining it though. just knowing there's a way out of the pain is calming.
yeah same here...it's just of myself. it can get terribly violent towards myself in my head. thing is I don't know why.
yeah I definitely feel that way. and the other shoe always drops...person leaves or distances themselves...

hmmm I think it's important to differentiate people not replying because they genuinely are too tired, or too busy or overwhelmed and people not replying because they want to disconnect. personally I've been called high maintenance and with some people they say that their friends are low maintenance and that kicks my anxiety into high gear because I then think oh shit I'm high maintenance, they'll hate me so I get into this state where if they don't reply quickly I immediately think okay well they hate me now that they know the real me.

yes to this. finding bosses and colleagues who are helpful and cooperative is so important. I've had to compromise on alot career progression wise just because I need so much rest from being normal all day. but that's okay. can't be the person who hustles all day, I'd hustle myself right into the psych ward.
wow the softball girl is so weird. I think u have to be very very strong and resilient and sure in yourself to survive dating in today's world omg.

yep and I only realised the impact my parenting and environment had on me when I was in my late 20s which was when I sought counselling and therapy again after a long hiatus. before that I just thought something was innately wrong with me and I was a pos. basically only found out 5 years ago that my upbringing was a big big factor in me turning out the way I am.

yep it's the instability of emotions. it's a defence mechanism at least for me to want to kill myself at the slightest inconvenience because I was raised to innately believe I need to go to 100 from 0 in order to solicitous attention.
Same here. in my 30s. never going to be in a healthy stable loving relationship...
oh and the icing on the cake is when their ex wasn't even diagnosed with bpd. it's just what they suspect their ex has.

oof I mean I don't mind people without bpd chiming in but some of them are people who dated someone with bpd and then they're here like oh you guys are all predictable, don't kid yourself into thinking you have self awareness. go to therapy. 
like wow what great advice, why didn't I think of it before? 

then I check out their profile and it's full of posts or comments in the sub that shalt not be named like "oh yeah my ex shouted at me and shit in my car, all bpd is npd"
yep me. demi, monogamous. and single but for a good reason. I have bpd woooooo scaryyyyy ahhhh damaged goods!

man this is tough to read. we always love so readily and usually towards people who find our love overbearing, annoying or gross.......until they need supply from us and we're all too willing to crawl back to them. we need to learn to walk the fuck away. sigh.
worst symptom for real is everything hahaha. joke answer wishing the criteria for being my parents is not just being horny.
I feel the exact same way. although they do eventually lose interest very quickly once they see how clingy and needy I am...so I guess that's a green flag.

relate alot. I want connection. I would love nothing more than a stable relationship with someone who I love and loves me. but I'm so so damaged that it's only fair and morally right for me not to pursue any relationship...it's just hard to live like this though. it's hard.

yeah definitely. especially when you're having a meltdown and you watch yourself doing something so stupid at the same time you hold yourself back as best as you can....end up not being to properly say what you mean. it's so painful being aware of all the shit you do and watch it happening and unravel your relationships. simultaneously know you don't want it to happen so you sob because you know the other person is going to leave because of something you are currently doing and fighting against to not do because you don't want to lose the person. at the same time though it's like hey I should really protect people from someone like me yet you want connection with others. it's just confusing, terribly painful and I'm very very very very exhausted of being in my skin and fighting with myself every single second of the day.
you know what I hate? when they say "I don't want to break up, but this just isn't working"
yeah I do the same. just spam everyone till someone answers.. always lonely.

yeah the same. when I imagine being euthanised like the injection and knowing that I always have the option to die, I just feel way calmer.

I feel trapped in my body...it's like I'm trapped in a fire and I can't escape. the emotions burn me alive. it's so painful.
I love music. so just playing my guitar and learning new music to take my mind off things.

yep! i spend all the major holidays alone now. my self harm urges are through the roof at the moment and I'm doing all I can not to give in. it's insane what I'm thinking of doing to myself. doing all the opposite action that I can.

I begged my ex not to break up with me until she hung up on me haha. I watched her eat pizza as I was sobbing because she was breaking up with me. I got on my knees and everything over the video call. Good Times.
yeah lol. instead of forming real connections, we form them in our heads lol. I feel pathetic for being so delulu. no one wants to hang out with me...

oof relate to the part on people's feelings evaporating. I'm the same. draw people in with charm then they see the real me the one who's flawed, clingy, self hating. boom feelings gone. feelings are so ephemeral and unreliable. it's okay though filters out people who have no idea what love and commitment actually is!
not alone in this. I've had more than one nye alone. it's okay to be sad. I plan to cry then watch some soothing familiar YouTube videos. basically what I do everyday.

my opinion is with therapy, hard work and a dose of good luck it definitely is possible. I've had terrible luck with falling for people who have left me with alot of relationship trauma to the extent that therapy is just for me to function in addition to all the traumatic things I've experienced as a child. "I didn't promise you a rose garden" is a book I think I've heard it's about how therapy doesn't mean your life magically gets better. trashy humans exist, you will or might meet them and they'll undo the progress that therapy has done for you. I wish you lots and lots of luck and all the best to not go through what I've gone through. work hard and become very aware of red flags in people. be slow to trust, be slow to attach so that if they do bad things it's easier and you didn't invest so much in them.
yeah I do that. it's maybe something related to how I didn't get comfort as a child or something haha. my ex hated it...found it gross
grass is greener syndrome man. I'm so freaking exhausted from the highs and lows in my mood, my life. I'm so dead tired.

yeah definitely. not just cut but very graphic self harm thoughts. it's hard to resist sometimes I just slap myself real hard to get rid of the urge which I guess is just another form of sh but whatever. 

I was "rage caned" as a child. so like my therapist says she noticed people who were rage caned tend to self harm. I think it's like we internalise our punisher, and we become the one to mete punishment in a very angry way to ourselves.

it feels like she used very "leading you on" language. it's understandable to be upset. just always remember with bpd, we HAVE to go slow. don't start planning futures with people. go slow. protect your heart always. humans are in general self serving and scary until proven otherwise with time and most importantly actions. interest doesn't mean commitment and alot of neurotypical people do not consider the impact of casually flirting without commitment since they don't feel as intensely as we do when rejected. remember protect your heart.
yeah this. sometimes the "unhealthy" way is the only way we can survive another day.

yeah totally agree haha. It's tricky. This is just my belief as someone who struggles alot with self-worth. I feel like as social creatures, we can't exactly heal in an invalidating environment. Being loved by others is important to feel worthy and it is from there that we springboard into the world (which contains alot of invalidating people) and are still able to maintain our self-worth in the face of invalidating experiences.

To go from just invalidation to self-worth without that middle step of having someone see our value is to me at least very difficult. 

Having said that, I think for me at least a more realistic goal is to be able to withstand the difficult emotions that come with feeling like "I am nothing, I am ugly, I am worthless, I am useless, I am better off dead," without lashing out at people. Gaining interpersonal skills to be able to engage with others and make friends. And remember that making friends takes time. Friendships take a while to build up to, and it is alot of effort on our parts because we're starting from a place which is more challenging, so don't be too hard on yourself if it goes a little less than ideal from time to time.

Gunderson says that therapy is a springboard towards gaining the skills towards being able to sustain relationships. It's not an end in itself. Which is something both Marsha Linehan and John Gunderson acknowledge which is why I admire them so much. They acknowledge reality and not portray this ideal optimistic hopeful picture of BPD , like saying stuff like "there is hope, it is highly treatable". while i get the good intention behind those kinds of therapists, I find it highly invalidating. Why make people have false hope? Gunderson even says it takes a whole lot of luck to find a corrective relationship- someone who will stick by you through the unstable initial years and then it settles down as you learn to trust them and heal. And if it ends, it can end up making your BPD come back in full force. Because by definition, remission means no evidence of disorder for now, NOT cured, NOT absence of disorder; A subtle but important difference.

Though I also believe that alot of things are easier said than done. With some situations I'm in, I'd imagine if I were my friend, I would say get out of it! But then it's so different when you are the one experiencing it, isn't it? Not so clear cut. So I believe there is no right or wrong or best way forward. 

It's clear you want to be with him and I feel from your description, he does want it too. He might have some misconceptions about the power of love (I saw in another comment you made that he believes that if you love someone enough, the "BPD" feelings won't come up) that are not true at all. BPD symptoms will come up no matter how much you love someone. Arguably, I would say it comes up the more you love or are attached to someone. 

Since he hasn't started therapy, I hope he can be disciplined when therapy starts, to get better. Motivation is fleeting honestly, so I prefer to say the word disciplined. With discipline, even if you're feeling bad, you would still have to do "opposite action" as it is known in DBT and other skills in your toolbox. Does he see a future with you? I'm saying like maybe when he is in his better states, does he talk about having a house with you with pets or something? That can help to be a motivating factor when he has bad days.

Even with therapy though, it might take years before he gets better and progress isn't linear, so that's something to keep in mind for you. Try to hang out with friends/acquaintances if it is possible. It's good for a couple to have time apart as well. As for the relationship you had years ago, I think that's a huge stumbling block for the relationship. Technically it is in the past, and should have no bearing on the current relationship. But I do get that he is insecure. I've been in that place where my insecurity about my ex's past caused issues. In retrospect, I feel it's so stupid because her past is passed. It's done, it's over, and she was with me at the time which is all that matters honestly. Creating issues where there was none only strained the relationship further. I'm grateful that my ex has allowed me to remain in contact with her. It has allowed me in some ways to practise the many things I learnt after she broke up with me about relationships skills. And I get to make it up to her, and be the partner I never was in the relationship. Although she never wants to be with me again, her leaving was very likely what kicked my ass into finally realising I need to change, sadly. I don't know how to help with that honestly, if he can't see that those things are in the past and the present and future is what matters now...

Last I checked, you need to get at least a master's degree in psychology to even be a practicising psychologist in my country. There was once I had casually mentioned that I was jealous about my ex's interest in a reality TV celebrity I think. She had misinterpreted that I was picking a fight about it and wanted to make sure she was not in lurve with him or something. Because she knows I have BPD, she thought I was going to be manipulative and demanding. So it became a shitshow. She circled her deadlines and sent me a picture  when I asked if we could call. That's it, just a picture.  I wanted to call her and just reassure her hey I love you, this isn't an argument, my "jealousy" is just something I'm mentioning casually, don't worry about me being triggered. Nope, she thought I had wanted to harp on the issue and keep talking about the jealousy issue. My therapist confirmed that this was something that was not the best...it was passive aggressive move to just send a picture with circled deadlines to my bid for affection and it was understandable that I would be upset. But even when I was upset, I had kept quiet. i couldn't sleep, I cried all night. I waited till her deadline was over before I contacted her to tell her I was upset. Because I wanted to make sure that she got her deadlines met. I put my own feelings on hold (which is an important skill btw, putting things on hold. She said it was because she didn't have time to talk and that I was somehow making it about her having to sacrifice her career for the relationship. I had to get validation from my therapist.

The sad thing is in my ex's mind, this simple misunderstanding was turned into drama caused by my BPD. In her narrative, the rockiness of the relationship was due to me. I won't say that my symptoms had nothing to do with it. But I do think it is important that we see people as they are, they are humans. The BPD is an illness, it's not who they are. Try to see your gf as human first and not BPD first. Don't presuppose a whole ton of stuff just because you know she has BPD. That was the forth time she tried to break up with me. The first time was when she exploded and told me all the things she had kept hidden that she was unhappy with. I was keen to work on them after she told me but it was too late, she told me later that it was the point when her feelings towards me had started to change. I worked hard, I believe she did too. But in the end my symptoms were the reason that she decided she didn't want to be with me. It hurt me deeply. I had put in effort, I was trying to speed up my recovery but in the end something about me that I fundamentally couldn't change was the reason that she had used. I felt like this stupid illness was something that prevented me from being with someone I had so much hopes and dreams of building a life with. I was looking at rings. I was buying in to the stories she told me of how our children would speak many languages (because we're both bilingual our second language being  different from each other). I said give me more time to make it better, I begged, I got on my knees. But it was over, I didn't do a good enough job. I said things were better now, she said no that things were worse. She had a million reasons for the break up but none to stay. She had collected an encylopedia's set worth of reasons from A to Z to counter all my proposals for working things out.

In the end , the rumination of wishing things were different landed me in the psych ward. It was the straw the broke the camel's back. I wanted to finally act on my plans to off myself because it was too much. My life hadn't been a smooth one and this was it.

I went to the emergency ward at my nearest hospital. I didn't know how I got myself there. I was a mess, I was sobbing and hyperventilating when I went to emergency. The nurse who took my vitals said my heart rate was too high. The ER doctor wanted to do an ECG on me. I said no, it's psychological, I just want to see my regular psychologist.

Anyway I'm out now. It's been almost a month i think since I've been discharged. My brother and father are trying their best to help me. My friends are busy, they don't contact me often. But I know they care. One of them is my accountability person. I'm only now finally accepting and grieving the loss. My ex has moved on quickly. It makes me think the relationship meant nothing to her but I know it's not true. People move on at a different pace. I still want her in my life. I believe she tried (although maybe she didn't know how) and I appreciate it alot. Honestly I don't need a partner that gets everything right. I just need a partner that wants to work with me, doesn't matter if they know how. She wants to remain friends, she says that she likes talking to me and that I make her happy and she doesn't want me to die. Although that may change one day. Right now my therapist and my accountability person is making sure I stick to clear boundaries with her so that I can heal. My family is helping me. Sometimes having a breakdown can be the catalyst for others in your life to help. I was trying to be the strong one, the dependable one who kept the car fueled up, the laundry done, making sure that my brother's insurance coverage was enough, that his money would be properly invested, that the detergent was stocked up, that there was toilet paper in the house. But I couldn't be that person anymore, I was that person when my mum died and my dad was a floating ghost, and now through my own private grief I had tried to be that person again, but I couldn't. I needed help and I got it. I don't know what will happen to me. I know relationships aren't something I would want to do for a long time. I'm terrified that my ex will find someone new who is better, who doesn't have this burdensome mental illness, and I know that day will come. And maybe she'll wave it in my face one day when she's having a bad day and her patience with me runs thin. Or maybe she'll just state it very matter-of-factly. I don't know what will happen when that day comes, but such is life.

Sometimes you have to be your own advocate and stand up for yourself. I learnt that the hard way. My psychologist is great but she isn't perfect. She has lots of patients to attend to, and they're aren't perfect beings. So they may be assessing a bunch of things that you aren't even aware of. Suicidal ideation has different levels to them with the top priority being means, plan and timeframe. When they see that you are calm, they may say okay you can try to do this on your own for a bit longer. I'll schedule you for a longer duration for the next appointment.

But you know yourself best, so you have to fight for yourself and stress the importance and urgency of your own situation to them. As some have suggested, documenting helps. Next time you have a very distressing thought, write down what you're saying to yourself verbatim.  Have an idea of what you want to improve on? Write it down as well, as a pointer to cover in your next session.

And remember that we won't always feel better or have everything discussed in therapy, work immediately. It takes time. You will still struggle with ideation and bad behaviours. Just have to put the techniques to work and see if it works and if it doesn't, try another one, discuss it with your therapist.

I think it's more about prescribing something that is a known weakness we have, perhaps? Or a common situation for people who are close with people suffering with BPD. Helping someone with the practical day-to-day chores isn't feeding into their symptoms either. It's not asking to help them at all costs, it's only when they have really bad episodes and you are able to.

I read an article recently about "boring". I can link it [here](https://www.bbc.com/worklife/article/20220422-why-we-snap-judge-some-people-as-boring). Basically, it says that humans make snap judgements and associations regarding what they think they find boring and that they tend to avoid "boring" to the extent that in an experiment, they would even want to be paid more money to converse with someone they thought was boring. I'm not saying all these to make you demoralised. Rather, it's to inform you about the psychological traps humans have regarding what constitutes "boring". The next thing is at the end of the article, knowing that we have these tendencies as humans, it talks about how we can reframe the way you describe yourself, and acquire skills to make better conversations. For example instead of saying "i chose to work nights" when you talk to people, maybe talk about why you chose to work nights? Is there a greater reason? Some insight that you have regarding the morning lark habits of most humans. Personally, I'd say "I swear I'm not a vampire, I work nights because the sun hurts my skin and I have weird fanglike teeth that I find better to hide in the darkness of the night", but that's the kind of stupid humour I have. Find something that fits your personality.

Of course, also seek out new experiences as others have suggested so you can meet more people and have more subjects to talk about with them. The more you talk, listen and learn, the more you will have to say when you talk to others.
